brief: Long, low general-store group at a rural crossroads: a two-storey gable-front frame store with a hip-roofed porch across its front on square posts, big display windows and a two-storey side wing with a gabled dormer, followed by a string of one-storey white frame outbuildings and a gabled garage along the highway. HABS drawings record the store; clapboard throughout, shade trees behind.

facade.notes: the D. H. Day Store (Glen Arbor MI, c.1900): a 1.5-storey frame general store, gable to the road, a full shed porch over two shop doors and windows, a gabled dormer, ivy up the side; small frame outbuildings beside

why.note: the frame general store of a lumber village: a house-shaped building with a porch for the shop
